title: Toussaint 1995: L3 and T9 erector spinae EMG (%SIC) and L5/S1 torque at maximal flexion during lifting
condition: dynamic lowering-lifting with a lifting device; task 1 no barbell, tasks 2-3 15.3 kg barbell

quantity.name: normalised ES EMG and L5/S1 torque at maximal flexion
quantity.definition: erector spinae EMG at L3 and T9 (3 cm lateral) normalised to angle-specific maximal isometric contraction (%SIC) at the instant of maximal flexion; net L5/S1 torque (Nm, linked-segment model); mean (SD)

source.authors: Toussaint HM, de Winter AF, de Haas Y, de Looze MP, van Dieen JH, Kingma I

protocol.summary: Lowering then lifting a barbell guided by a lifting device (lowest level 19.5 cm or 29.4 cm = 30% of leg length); EMG normalised per L5/S1 angle with isometric maxima over 9 trunk angles.
how_to_simulate: Scale to male, 21.8 y, 184 cm, 70.8 kg
Posture at maximal flexion of the lowering-lifting cycle (L5/S1 flexion ~55 deg, hip ~40 deg)
Hand load: none (task 1) or 15.3 kg barbell held in both hands at 19.5 cm (task 2) or 29.4 cm (task 3) above the floor
Output: L3-level vs T9-level ES activation (%) and net L5/S1 moment
protocol.notes: Electrodes Ag-AgCl 3 cm lateral to midline at T9, L1, L3, L5 (+ 6 cm lateral at L3); L1, L3, L5 very similar. Barbell mass 15.3 kg in Table 1 (15.4 kg in figure captions). FR at L3 begins ~30% of movement time while T9 EMG rises to ~105% SIC (text).

data.x: task 2 (15.3 kg, lowest 19.5 cm): L3 EMG
task 3 (15.3 kg, lowest 29.4 cm): L3 EMG

extraction.check_notes: Scanned PDF; Table 2 checked against the page image (p.206).

pass_rule.rule: |model - mean| <= 1 SD (angles); for SEM-reported data use SD = SEM x sqrt(n)
